newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kaifa says profit soars on tech upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Kaifa says profit soars on tech upgrade.

text.p: Shenzhen Kaifa Technology Co Ltd said on Friday that upgraded technology helped the company to achieve a 133 percent surge in post-tax profits in 1996.

"Kaifa injected 145 million yuan to upgrade technology in 1996 and has 140 million yuan reserved for 1997," the computer components maker said in its 1996 annual report published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The company's 1996 net profit surged to 275.37 million yuan from 118.35 million yuan in 1995, said Kaifa, which has two ventures in Shenzhen with International Business Machines Corp.
The per-share net was 1.037 yuan against 0.624 yuan in 1995 and turnover was 1.62 billion yuan against 1.60 billion yuan, it said.
The quality of the firm's 30 million hard drive components produced in 1996, 99.9 percent of which were exported, carried higher added value, the Kaifa annual report said but did not elaborate.
Company officials reached by telephone declined to comment.

Kaifa's computer parts ventures with IBM are the $20 million Shenzhen Hailiang Storage Product Co Ltd and $9 million Shenzhen Changke International Electronics Co Ltd, according to Kaifa's 1996 annual report.
IBM has a 75 percent stake in Hailiang, set up in March 1996 with China Great Wall Computer Group Co, which holds 15 percent, and Kaifa, which owns 10 percent, a Kaifa spokesman said earlier.
Changke is 60 percent owned by IBM and 25 percent by Great Wall, and Kaifa paid US$1.35 million to buy a 15 percent stake in 1995, the spokesman said.
Trading in Kaifa's A shares was suspended on Friday morning on posting of the annual results and it resumed in the afternoon.
On Thursday, Kaifa's A shares ended at 37.53 yuan, up from 18.10 yuan at the beginning of 1997, largely due to expectations of strong 1996 results, brokers said.

Kaifa said its board of directors proposed to offer a 10-for-10 bonus issue plus a 0.2 yuan per share cash dividend for all shareholders from its profits in 1996, pending the approval of shareholders at a meeting scheduled for May 5.
